key_insight: Pareto-aware decision-focused learning trains predictions to support multi-objective decisions rather than prediction accuracy alone.
engineering_relevance: The approach could improve logistics, routing, and resource allocation plans that must balance conflicting objectives under predicted costs.
method: Extend single-objective SPO+ to multi-objective combinatorial optimization.
Use the true Pareto Frontier and a sampled preference vector to form a target decision.
Train by minimizing regret against that target.
evidence_signal: Experiments on multi-objective shortest path and knapsack problems report improvements over MSE-trained two-stage models and scalarization-based SPO+, without quantitative results in the abstract.
watch_item: Dependence on the true Pareto Frontier may make training computationally challenging for larger problems.
paper_title: Pareto-Informed Smart "Predict, then Optimize" for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Problems
